title: Honest Adaptive Intervals for Regenerative Policy Evaluation across Nested Overlap Classes
banked_reason: The valid-witness failure cannot be bounded because the frozen acceptance relation does not imply a dominating valid candidate with no larger realized radius.
gap_reasons: The valid-witness failure cannot be bounded because the frozen acceptance relation does not imply a dominating valid candidate with no larger realized radius.
Coverage and componentwise expected length for the specific frozen selector C_T^{ad} remain unproved.
The proposed maximal-envelope procedure is mathematically coherent as a fixed broad-class interval, but it removes the field-tier novelty kernel that justified this run.
proof_attempt_summary: The original critical-logarithm minimax claim contradicted the Hu–Wager equality-case benchmark, so discovery pivoted to confidence-interval adaptation across reset and overlap classes. The finite-sample selector did not establish broad-class coverage and componentwise short length; a fixed maximal-envelope interval survived as a conservative below-field result. A future specialization could use the known policies to compute the overlap constant, reduce to one unknown reset parameter, and develop a new class-targeted interval or reachable-support impossibility pair.
tldr: The nested-class bookkeeping and the law-indexed regenerative score bound are proved. A separate maximal-envelope score interval is finite-sample honest, has an explicit computable threshold ensuring \(b_T\ge1\), and has the displayed broad-envelope expected-length bound. The frozen adaptive selector is not yet certified: center agreement does not imply the radius ordering required by its valid-witness event, so neither its factor-five coverage nor its componentwise length theorem is claimed. The optimal cross-class penalty remains open after a source-faithful audit.
gap: HuWager2023 Section 4 supplies asymptotic Lepski selection but not finite-sample coverage over a broad canonical union or simultaneous componentwise expected-length control. CaiLow2004 supplies the relevant adaptation geometry only for Gaussian linear-functional experiments.
fill: The project studies one executable robust interval with broad-union coverage and the exact componentwise score-radius bound, and it leaves recovery of a root-\(T\) critical adaptive rate to a separately stated modulus-and-score question.
